details.description: LLaVA-v1.6-34B (also called LLaVA-NeXT-34B) is an open chatbot from Haotian Liu's LLaVA project, fine-tuned from NousResearch's Nous-Hermes-2-Yi-34B, which is itself built on 01.AI's Yi-34B base model. It was released January 30, 2024, trained on roughly 1.3 million instruction-following examples drawn from LAION, GPT-generated data, and academic datasets, and is licensed Apache 2.0 (inherited from its base model). It serves chat completions with a 4,096-token context window.
advantages: The LLaVA project's GitHub repository states that LLaVA-NeXT-34B outperforms Google's Gemini Pro on some benchmarks.
Fine-tuned on about 1.3 million instruction-following examples drawn from LAION, GPT-generated data, and academic datasets, per its Hugging Face model card.
Open weights under the Apache 2.0 license, inherited from its Yi-34B base.
disadvantages: 4,096-token context window, small for a model this size.
use_cases: Research and experimentation with open, large (34B-parameter) instruction-tuned checkpoints

notes: Catalog facts list a 4,096-token, text-only (text_input/text_output) modality for this entry, which matches the context window I found (4.09k on Fireworks' page) but not the modality: LLaVA-v1.6-34B is fundamentally a vision-language checkpoint (image + text input) per its GitHub repo and Hugging Face card. I did not state image input as a capability here, per the instruction to keep the catalog's modality value -- but flagging this as a significant discrepancy for review, since visual question answering is this checkpoint's whole purpose. Confirmed 'llava-yi-34b' on Fireworks = liuhaotian/llava-v1.6-34b (base: NousResearch/Nous-Hermes-2-Yi-34B, built on 01-ai/Yi-34B) via Fireworks' own description ('fine-tuned version of the Yi 34B LLM') and the matching 4,096-token context window. No numeric benchmark scores found on any page I opened (the LLaVA GitHub repo references 'LLaVA-NeXT-34B outperforms Gemini Pro on some benchmarks' without giving numbers), so evaluations is empty. Verification pass: corrected the release date from 'December 2023' to January 30, 2024 -- the GitHub repo's changelog dates the LLaVA-NeXT (v1.6) announcement to '1/30', the blog post is dated 2024-01-30, and the Hugging Face repo was created 2024-01-31; December 2023 appears to be when training/data collection happened, not the public release.
